transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 PT (42 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - AsterCare), Priya Desai (Platform Eng), Monica Reyes (Security), Evan Park (DevOps)

Summary (auto-generated):
Quick walkthrough of Redwood's rate limiting, quotas, and org/project key model. Focus on multi-tenant controls, per-project usage isolation, RBAC mapping, and how rate limits are surfaced in the Console and API. Customer asked security and compliance questions (SOC2, KMS), and requested a sandbox org with project keys and pricing follow-up.

Topics: rate limits, org keys, project keys, quotas, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2/KMS, pilot/benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro — I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with me is Maya from our solutions eng team.
[00:12] Maya: hi all, Maya Chen, I'll run through the console demo and the API bits for org + project keys, please stop me with questions.
[00:20] Liam: yep thanks, wanted to get straight into how you handle rate limiting multi-tenant, we run multi-tenant workloads and want per-customer quotas.
[00:31] Jordan: totally, that's a common pattern — we'll show our org/project key model which lets you map projects to customers and apply granular quotas and rate limits per project, per route.
[00:45] Maya: jumping into the console — so here's the org view, you can see overall org usage, then we have project keys under Projects, each project gets a unique API key and optional metadata tags — you can attach customer-id. we also support project-level quotas (monthly tokens, concurrent requests) and route-level rate limits.
[01:10] Priya: is there an API to create projects and keys? we want to automate provisioning during our onboarding flow.
[01:16] Maya: yes, we have a Projects API, plus SDK helpers. Example curl to create a project and key is in the docs — we can automate rotate keys and attach RBAC rules.
[01:30] Evan: how do you enforce strict limits? if a customer bursts, do other projects get impacted?
[01:38] Maya: enforcement is hierarchical — org-level pool, then project quotas. if a single project hits its limit, we return 429 for that key and optionally forward to a fallback policy if configured. other projects are isolated unless org pool exhausted. we also do fair-share on GPU-backed Dedicated pools.
[01:58] Monica: on the security side, we need audit logs and key rotation proof for compliance. where are logs stored?
[02:06] Jordan: good question — we provide per-request audit logs, you can stream them to your SIEM or request log export. for Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem or ship to a customer-managed S3.
[02:20] Monica: and encryption keys — do you integrate with our KMS?
[02:24] Maya: yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted has an option for customer-managed keys in some regions. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[02:35] Liam: ok, can you show how rate limits surface in telemetry? we need visibility per customer and alerting thresholds.
[02:41] Maya: switching to Optimize tab — we have token breakdown by project and route, and per-key latency percentiles. you can create alerts on error rate or rate-limit saturation. here we have example dashboards — in the console you can filter by project key and time window and export CSV.
[03:05] Jordan: note also we emit traces you can hook with our tracing hooks so you correlate request id down to the model and kernel selection.
[03:14] Priya: model variants — does fallback to smaller/cheaper model happen automatically when a project is throttled or when capacity constrained?
[03:21] Maya: we support smart routing and automatic fallback policies; you can configure route policies to fallback to a compatible quantized model variant to preserve availability. that's part of our graceful degradation suite.
[03:37] Evan: i heard earlier mention of autoscaling and burst capacity — how does that interact with reserved quotas?
[03:44] Jordan: reserved capacity (Dedicated) gives guaranteed throughput; you can also allow burst on shared capacity subject to org-level caps. quotas are orthogonal — you still enforce per-project token limits.
[03:55] Liam: what happens if someone shares an org key accidentally? can we quickly rotate?
[04:00] Maya: keys can be rotated via API or the console; we support immediate revoke and issue new keys. we also have short-lived keys options for ephemeral workloads.
[04:12] Liam: ok that's useful.
[04:14] Maya: quick note — in the demo console i created example project 'astercare-patient-nlp' and a project key with tag customer=astercare, you can see applied quota of 5M tokens/month and a burst window limit of 10 qps.
[04:31] Priya: is throttling per-second or sliding window?
[04:35] Maya: both — we support fixed-window and sliding-window rate limit configs, and token-based quotas for monthly usage.
[04:42] Monica: audit trail again — can you show an example entry?
[04:45] Maya: sure, here's an example log line — timestamp, project_id, key_id, user_id, route, tokens_used, latency_ms; small caveat the agent sometimes labels k-v cache as 'kv cash' in the export hehe.
[05:03] Liam: haha ok noted.
[05:05] Jordan: switching to API — sample request with project key in header, you'll see 200/streaming or 429 depending on state. i'll run a quick curl to show a 429 test.
[05:18] [demo noise — terminal click]
[05:22] Jordan: ok i triggered a test client that exceeds qps and you can see 429 body has rate_limit: {limit, remaining, reset} plus helpful headers x-rate-limit-remaining etc.
[05:36] Priya: those headers are good for our client retry logic. what about global vs per-route limits?
[05:42] Maya: each route can have independent limits, and you can combine with model-specific quotas — e.g., captioning model might have a different per-token cost and limits.
[05:54] Evan: does Redwood's billing align with project keys? we need invoicing per-customer.
[06:01] Jordan: yes — billing can be broken down by project and tag, you can export per-project usage for chargeback. for Dedicated we support committed spend and per-project metering.
[06:14] Liam: sounds good. can you confirm data residency? we have EU patients and need logs/data to stay in EU region for certain projects.
[06:24] Maya: region-scoped projects are supported in Private and Dedicated; hosted API has region selection for data residency in some cases. for strict residency we recommend Private.
[06:35] Monica: any customers using Redwood Inf... sorry Redwood Infference in regulated healthcare?
[06:41] Jordan: yes we have a couple — we'll anonymize references but share case studies.
[06:47] Priya: Ok let's talk about SSO and RBAC mapping — can we tie project keys to Okta groups?
[06:55] Maya: you can map RBAC roles to teams, and project keys can be scoped. for admin operations we recommend SAML SSO and granular RBAC. we have examples for Okta SCIM provisioning.
[07:10] Liam: excellent.
[07:12] Jordan: quick deeper question from Maya to address technical: are you more concerned about burst protection or long tail billing surprises?
[07:20] Priya: long tail billing surprises — we had one customer last quarter that had a runaway pipeline and racked up costs.
[07:26] Maya: for that we recommend hard monthly quotas at project level plus billing alerts; Optimize will suggest token-saving quantization profiles for high-volume endpoints.
[07:40] Evan: about pilot — we want to bench CPU vs GPU cost tradeoffs and measure p95 latency with our prompt sets.
[07:48] Jordan: we can run a 2-week benchmark in the sandbox org using your prompt set, collect latency and token cost, and produce an optimization checklist: batching settings, quantization, kernel hints.
[07:59] Liam: timeline — we're targeting pilot in Jan, enterprise procurement in Feb.
[08:05] Jordan: that works, we'll try to get pilot kick off before end of year if possible.
[08:11] Monica: any lock-in concerns — if we go Dedicated then later go Private how seamless is migration?
[08:18] Maya: same APIs and config layer across modes; model versions and rollout policies can be pinned and migrated, but Private has some additional ops work. in practice migration is mainly infra integration.
[08:35] Priya: can you remind us about org-level fallback? if org pool is exhausted do you block or fallback to shared?
[08:42] Jordan: fallback policies are configurable — can block, queue, or route to a degraded model on shared capacity. policies can be set per-project or org-wide.
[08:55] Evan: any guidance on quota numbers for multi-tenant — how do you size?
[08:59] Maya: we look at historical token distribution, 95th percentile bursts, and apply safety buffers. Optimize gives suggestions after initial telemetry.
[09:12] [15-minute mark — demo continues with Console walkthrough of policy creation]
[09:30] Jordan: small note about naming — our dashboard sometimes shows project ids not friendly names in export, we recommend tagging early.
[09:40] Priya: we will do that.
[09:44] Monica: security again — you mentioned SIEM shipping, can we S3 to our internal bucket with lifecycle policies?
[09:52] Maya: yes, you can configure log sinks to a customer S3 with customer-managed keys.
[09:58] Liam: ok anything else on compliance?
[10:02] Jordan: we'll send SOC2 + encryption docs, and Maya will include KMS integration steps.
[10:08] [demo: running a small script to show per-project breakdown]
[10:20] Maya: here you can see a spike in tokens for project astercare-patient-nlp, you can click into the request row and see the user agent and route, and kick off a revoke if needed.
[10:36] Evan: that revoke UI will help with keys leaked.
[10:40] Priya: question on SDKs — do you support server-side and mobile short-lived keys?
[10:45] Maya: yes, we have short-lived JWT issuance via the Projects API, mobile can use ephemeral tokens.
[10:52] Monica: how granular are the audit events for token usage? we need per-request identity linking.
[10:57] Maya: we include request_id, project_id, user_id if available, and you can attach correlation_id from your layer.
[11:06] Liam: thanks — that addresses a lot.
[11:09] Jordan: i know we're near end, quick recap and next steps — we'll share pricing, security pack, and a sandbox org. Maya will provision a sandbox with two projects and sample keys for your infra team to run the benchmark.
[11:25] Priya: confirm who will get the sandbox creds?
[11:28] Maya: i'll send to Liam and Priya only, cc Jordan.
[11:33] Liam: ok, and timeline? pilot kickoff week of Jan 12 works for us.
[11:39] Jordan: great, we'll target that.
[11:42] Monica: one last question — do rate-limit headers include reset in ms?
[11:46] Maya: yes reset is in seconds by default, you can opt for ms in the header.
[11:51] Evan: nice.
[11:53] Jordan: cool, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
[12:00] [meeting end — 42 minutes recorded]
